folder_html:
LIVE CHLOROPHYLL / ALGAL ACTIVITY

Chlorophyll-a concentration at the lake surface, a proxy for phytoplankton abundance/biomass. NOT a toxin measurement and NOT a harmful-algal-bloom diagnosis.

Chlorophyll-a concentration (mg/m^3), continuous: LOWEST 0.159 (dark blue) → common 1 (green/yellow) → HIGHEST+ 99.93 (deep purple). High values compress into red/purple; they indicate biomass/activity, not toxins.

Units: mg/m^3
Source: NOAA CoastWatch S-NPP VIIRS chlorophyll-a, Science Quality, Global 4 km, Daily (ERDDAP nesdisVHNSQchlaDaily)
Update: daily composites
Data time: 2026-09-12T12:00:00Z (mosaic 2026-09-12..2026-09-10)
Processed: 2026-09-22 03:16 UTC
Why high values turn red/purple: Very high values (blooms, algal activity, turbid intrusions) compress into red-violet/deep-purple; common background concentrations own most of the color resolution.
